questions.stem: Who is popularly known as the Father of the Nation in India?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi is called the Father of the Nation because he led the non-violent freedom struggle through movements such as Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience and Quit India, and guided millions of Indians towards independence in 1947.

optionRationale.1: Nehru was the first Prime Minister, not the Father of the Nation.
optionRationale.3: Patel is remembered as the Iron Man of India for uniting the princely states.
optionRationale.4: Bose led the Indian National Army and is called Netaji.

questions.objective: Identify the Father of the Nation

questions.stem: Which animal is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The Bengal tiger is the national animal of India. It was chosen as a symbol of strength, grace and power, and Project Tiger, launched in 1973, protects it and its habitats in reserves across the country.

optionRationale.1: The Asiatic lion is found only in Gir and is on the national emblem, but it is not the national animal.
optionRationale.2: The elephant is the national heritage animal, a different title.
optionRationale.3: The leopard is a big cat but has no national status.

questions.stem: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh square kilometres and is the largest Indian state by area. Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra follow it, while Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state but much smaller in area than Rajasthan.

optionRationale.1: Madhya Pradesh is second in area, not first.
optionRationale.2: Maharashtra is third in area.
optionRationale.4: Uttar Pradesh is first in population, not in area.

questions.objective: Recall the largest state by area

questions.stem: The river Ganga finally flows into which water body?
questions.explanation: After flowing across the northern plains and joining the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh, the Ganga forms the large Sundarbans delta and empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Arabian Sea receives rivers such as the Narmada and Tapi.

optionRationale.1: The Arabian Sea receives west-flowing rivers like the Narmada, not the Ganga.
optionRationale.2: Kochi lies on the Kerala coast and no Ganga branch reaches it.
optionRationale.4: The Gulf of Kutch is on the Gujarat coast, far from the Ganga system.

questions.objective: Locate the mouth of the Ganga

questions.stem: Who was the first President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who had also presided over the Constituent Assembly, became the first President of India when the Constitution came into force in 1950. He served two terms, until 1962.

optionRationale.1: Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President and the second President.
optionRationale.3: Zakir Husain became President later, in 1967.
optionRationale.4: V. V. Giri served as President in 1969-74, long after the first.

questions.stem: National Science Day in India is celebrated every year on
questions.explanation: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February to mark the announcement of the Raman Effect by Sir C. V. Raman in 1928, a discovery for which he later received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

optionRationale.1: 5 September is Teachers' Day.
optionRationale.2: 15 August is Independence Day.
optionRationale.3: 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti.

questions.objective: Recall the date of National Science Day

questions.stem: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra in the Indian national flag have?
questions.explanation: The navy-blue Ashoka Chakra at the centre of the white band has 24 spokes. It is taken from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath and stands for the wheel of law and continuous progress.

optionRationale.1: 12 is half the real number and is not used.
optionRationale.2: 16 does not match the flag.
optionRationale.4: 32 is more than the 24 spokes of the Chakra.

questions.objective: Recall the features of the national flag

questions.stem: Which is the largest ocean of the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers roughly one third of the Earth's surface and is larger than all the land area of the world put together. It is also the deepest ocean, containing the Mariana Trench.

optionRationale.1: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.
optionRationale.3: The Indian Ocean is the third largest.
optionRationale.4: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest ocean.

questions.stem: In which city is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India located?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, the central bank that issues currency and controls credit, was set up in 1935 and has its central office in Mumbai. It has regional offices in other cities, including New Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai.

optionRationale.1: New Delhi hosts the Finance Ministry but not the RBI central office.
optionRationale.2: Kolkata was the first office of the bank but it later moved to Mumbai.
optionRationale.3: Chennai has only a regional office.

questions.stem: Teachers' Day in India is celebrated every year on
questions.explanation: Teachers' Day is observed on 5 September, the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a philosopher-teacher who became the second President of India. It is a day of respect for all teachers who shape students in schools and colleges.

optionRationale.1: 14 November is Children's Day, the birthday of Jawaharlal Nehru.
optionRationale.2: 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti.
optionRationale.3: 26 January is Republic Day.

questions.objective: Recall the date of Teachers' Day

questions.stem: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari, about 1,465 km long, is the longest river of peninsular India and is often called the Dakshin Ganga. It rises near Nashik in Maharashtra and falls into the Bay of Bengal.

optionRationale.2: The Krishna is longer than the Kaveri but shorter than the Godavari.
optionRationale.3: The Kaveri is much shorter.
optionRationale.4: The Narmada flows west to the Arabian Sea and is shorter.

questions.stem: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee that prepared the draft of the Constitution, and he is therefore known as its chief architect. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly itself.

optionRationale.1: Rajendra Prasad presided over the whole Assembly, not the Drafting Committee.
optionRationale.2: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution but did not chair the committee.
optionRationale.4: Munshi was a member of the Drafting Committee only.

questions.stem: Which Prime Minister gave the slogan "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan"?
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" during the 1965 war with Pakistan and a food shortage, to honour soldiers who guard the border and farmers who feed the nation.

optionRationale.1: Nehru is linked to "Aram Haram Hai" and planning.
optionRationale.3: Indira Gandhi is linked to "Garibi Hatao".
optionRationale.4: Morarji Desai did not give this slogan.

questions.stem: The Battle of Plassey, which strengthened the rule of the East India Company in Bengal, was fought in the year
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between Robert Clive of the Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal. The Nawab lost because of the betrayal of Mir Jafar, and the Company became a political power in Bengal.

optionRationale.1: 1707 is the year Aurangzeb died.
optionRationale.2: 1764 is the year of the Battle of Buxar.
optionRationale.3: 1857 is the year of the Great Revolt.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form, making its enforcement an offence punishable by law. It is part of the Right to Equality in Part III of the Constitution.

optionRationale.2: Article 14 gives equality before the law.
optionRationale.3: Article 15 forbids discrimination on grounds such as religion, race and caste.
optionRationale.4: Article 19 lists freedoms such as speech and movement.

questions.stem: Match List-I (cities) with List-II (rivers on whose banks they stand).
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad is on the Sabarmati (IV), Kolkata on the Hooghly (III), Nashik on the Godavari (II) and Vijayawada on the Krishna (I). So the correct code is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

optionRationale.1: It swaps the Sabarmati and the Hooghly.
optionRationale.2: It swaps the Godavari and the Krishna.
optionRationale.4: It gives Ahmedabad the Godavari and Nashik the Sabarmati.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights in India.
A. Article 21 protects the right to life and personal liberty.
B. The right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years is part of Article 21A.
C. The right to property is a Fundamental Right under Article 31.
D. Article 32 gives the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements A, B and D are correct. Article 21 protects life and liberty, Article 21A gives education for children aged 6 to 14, and Article 32 is the remedy for enforcement. Statement C is wrong because the right to property was removed from Part III in 1978 and is now only a legal right under Article 300A.

optionRationale.1: It omits B and D, which are correct, and includes C, which is wrong.
optionRationale.3: It includes C, which is wrong, and omits A.
optionRationale.4: It includes C, which is no longer a Fundamental Right.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The Himalayan rivers such as the Ganga carry water throughout the year.
Reason (R): The Himalayan rivers are fed both by rainfall and by melting of snow and glaciers.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Himalayan rivers have snow and glaciers at their source in addition to monsoon rain, so the supply continues in the dry season. This is why they are perennial, unlike many peninsular rivers that depend only on rain.

optionRationale.2: R is the actual reason for A, so it is not a mere unrelated truth.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so this option cannot hold.
optionRationale.4: R is true, so this option cannot hold.

questions.objective: Explain why Himalayan rivers are perennial

questions.stem: The Dronacharya Award is given in India for
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award honours coaches who have trained sportspersons to achieve international success. Players receive the Arjuna Award and the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, while civil bravery awards are separate.

optionRationale.1: That describes the Arjuna Award, which is for players.
optionRationale.2: Arts are honoured by the Sangeet Natak Akademi awards and the Padma awards.
optionRationale.3: Bravery in saving lives is honoured by the Jeevan Raksha awards.

questions.objective: Recall the purpose of national sports awards

questions.stem: In which year did C. V. Raman receive the Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.explanation: Sir C. V. Raman discovered the scattering of light now called the Raman Effect in 1928 and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for it in 1930, becoming the first Asian to win a Nobel in the sciences.

optionRationale.2: 1928 is the year of the discovery, not the award.
optionRationale.3: 1947 is the year of Indian independence.
optionRationale.4: 1954 is not the year of his Nobel Prize.

questions.objective: Date C. V. Raman's Nobel Prize

questions.stem: Human Rights Day is observed every year on
questions.explanation: Human Rights Day marks 10 December 1948, the day the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which sets out the basic rights of every person. It is observed worldwide and reminds people of basic freedoms.

optionRationale.1: 24 October is United Nations Day.
optionRationale.2: 1 December is observed as World AIDS Day.
optionRationale.4: 25 December is Christmas.

questions.objective: Recall the date of Human Rights Day

questions.stem: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: Anamudi, in the Anamalai range of Kerala, rises to about 2,695 m and is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris.

optionRationale.1: Doddabetta is high but lower than Anamudi.
optionRationale.3: Mahendragiri belongs to the Eastern Ghats.
optionRationale.4: Mount Abu is in the Aravalli range of Rajasthan.

questions.objective: Identify the highest peak of the Western Ghats

questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline on the mainland?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest mainland coastline of any Indian state, more than 1,600 km along the Arabian Sea including the Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu follow with shorter coasts.

optionRationale.1: Tamil Nadu has a long coast but a shorter one than Gujarat.
optionRationale.2: Maharashtra's coast is about 720 km, well below Gujarat's.
optionRationale.3: Andhra Pradesh is second, not first.

questions.stem: Emperor Ashoka gave up war and embraced Buddhism after the war against
questions.explanation: The bloody conquest of Kalinga, in present-day Odisha, around 261 BCE filled Ashoka with remorse. He gave up conquest by war and adopted Buddhism and the policy of dhamma, which he recorded in his rock edicts.

optionRationale.2: Gandhara was in the north-west and not the cause of his change.
optionRationale.3: Magadha was his own kingdom.
optionRationale.4: Avanti was a Mauryan province, not the site of the war.

questions.stem: What is the minimum age to vote in elections in India?
questions.explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment of 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, which came into effect in 1989. A citizen must be 18 and registered in the electoral roll to vote.

optionRationale.1: 16 years is not the legal voting age.
optionRationale.2: 21 years was the voting age before 1989.
optionRationale.4: 25 years is the minimum age to contest Lok Sabha elections.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is in
questions.explanation: ISRO has its headquarters in Bengaluru. Sriharikota is only the launch centre in Andhra Pradesh, and Thiruvananthapuram hosts the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre. Launch vehicles are flown from the spaceport at Sriharikota, but administration is run from the headquarters.

optionRationale.1: Sriharikota is the launch site, not the headquarters.
optionRationale.3: Thiruvananthapuram has a major centre but not the headquarters.
optionRationale.4: Hyderabad hosts the National Remote Sensing Centre.

questions.stem: The national song "Vande Mataram" was written by
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Vande Mataram in the 1870s, and it later appeared in his novel Anandamath. It became a rallying song of the freedom movement and is the national song of India.

optionRationale.1: Tagore wrote the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
optionRationale.2: Iqbal wrote the song "Saare Jahan Se Achha".
optionRationale.3: Subramania Bharati was a Tamil poet of patriotic songs.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization, a specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1948, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The UN itself sits in New York. Remember that WHO deals with global health, while the UN General Assembly meets in New York.

optionRationale.2: New York is home to the UN headquarters.
optionRationale.3: Paris hosts UNESCO.
optionRationale.4: Vienna hosts agencies such as the IAEA.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations.
A. It was founded in 1945.
B. Its headquarters is in New York.
C. The Security Council has 12 members in all.
D. The Security Council has five permanent members.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The UN was founded in 1945 (A), has its headquarters in New York (B) and the Security Council has five permanent members (D). Statement C is wrong because the Council has 15 members: five permanent and ten elected non-permanent members.

optionRationale.1: It omits D, which is correct.
optionRationale.2: It includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: It includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out B.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on the United Nations

questions.stem: Arrange these battles in chronological order: (1) Battle of Plassey, (2) First Battle of Panipat, (3) Battle of Buxar, (4) Battle of Haldighati.
questions.explanation: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526, Haldighati in 1576, Plassey in 1757 and Buxar in 1764. So the right sequence is 2, 4, 1, 3. Writing the dates side by side makes the order easy to check.

optionRationale.1: It puts Plassey before Haldighati, which is wrong.
optionRationale.3: It puts Haldighati before Panipat, which is wrong.
optionRationale.4: It puts Buxar before Plassey, but Buxar came later, in 1764.

questions.stem: Match List-I (Articles of the Constitution) with List-II (subject).

right: I. Protection of life and personal liberty
IV. Freedom of speech and expression

questions.explanation: Article 14 gives equality before law (III), Article 19 gives the freedoms including speech and expression (IV), Article 21 protects life and personal liberty (I), and Article 32 gives the right to constitutional remedies (II). So the code is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

optionRationale.1: It swaps Articles 19 and 21.
optionRationale.2: It swaps Articles 14 and 19.
optionRationale.3: It swaps Articles 21 and 32.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The Constitution of India is described as partly rigid and partly flexible.
Reason (R): Some provisions can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament, while others need a special majority, and a few also need ratification by the States.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and R explains A. Article 368 provides for different methods of amendment: some changes need only a simple majority, others a special majority, and federal features additionally need approval by half of the State legislatures, mixing flexibility and rigidity.

optionRationale.2: R is the direct reason for A, so it is the correct explanation.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about India's geography.
A. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Madhya Pradesh.
B. The Standard Meridian of India, 82.5 degrees East, passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
C. Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich time.
D. India has two standard meridians, one for the east and one for the west.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Madhya Pradesh (A), the Standard Meridian 82.5 degrees E passes near Mirzapur (B), and IST is UTC+5:30 (C). Statement D is wrong since India uses a single standard time and one standard meridian for the whole country.

optionRationale.2: It includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out B and C.
optionRationale.3: It includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: It includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out C.

questions.stem: The Indus Valley site of Dholavira, noted for its water conservation system, is located in which present-day Indian state?
questions.explanation: Dholavira lies on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat and is known for its large reservoirs and channels. Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, Rakhigarhi in Haryana, and Mohenjo-daro in Pakistan.

optionRationale.1: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, not Dholavira.
optionRationale.2: Rakhigarhi and Banawali are in Haryana.
optionRationale.4: Ropar is the Harappan site in Punjab.

questions.stem: Match List-I (reform organisations) with List-II (founders).
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (III), Swami Dayananda Saraswati the Arya Samaj (IV), Swami Vivekananda the Ramakrishna Mission (I) and Jyotirao Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj (II). So the code is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

optionRationale.1: It swaps the founders of the Brahmo Samaj and the Arya Samaj.
optionRationale.3: It gives the Arya Samaj to Vivekananda and the Mission to Dayananda.
optionRationale.4: It swaps Vivekananda and Phule.

questions.stem: Which of the following words were added to the Preamble of the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment of 1976?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment inserted the words Socialist and Secular and the word Integrity into the Preamble. Sovereign, Democratic and Republic, and the ideals of justice, liberty and equality, were in the original Preamble.

optionRationale.1: These three words were there from the start.
optionRationale.2: These ideals were also part of the original Preamble.
optionRationale.3: Federal and Unity were not added in this way.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the judiciary of India.
A. Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of 65 years.
B. Judges of the High Courts retire at the age of 62 years.
C. Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President.
D. Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of 62 years.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 (A), High Court judges at 62 (B), and Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President (C). Statement D contradicts A and is false, since 62 is the High Court retirement age.

optionRationale.2: It leaves out C, which is correct.
optionRationale.3: It includes D, which is false, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: It includes D, which is false, and leaves out B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following Indian states does NOT share a border with Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Himachal Pradesh borders Tibet (China) and other Indian states but not Nepal. Remember the five bordering states as Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim.

optionRationale.1: Sikkim borders Nepal on the west.
optionRationale.2: Bihar borders Nepal on the north.
optionRationale.4: Uttarakhand borders Nepal on the east.

questions.stem: Who presided over the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in 1929, which declared Purna Swaraj as its goal?
questions.explanation: At the Lahore Session in December 1929, held under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress declared complete independence (Purna Swaraj) as its goal, and 26 January 1930 was fixed as Independence Day.

optionRationale.1: Gandhi did not preside at Lahore, though he led the movement.
optionRationale.3: Motilal Nehru presided in 1928 at Calcutta.
optionRationale.4: Bose was a young leader, not the president that year.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) Secretariat is located in
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal, and was established there in 1987. The organisation was founded in 1985 at Dhaka, but the secretariat was placed in Kathmandu. The two cities are therefore not the same, which is a common trap.

optionRationale.1: New Delhi is not the seat of the secretariat.
optionRationale.2: Colombo is not the seat of the secretariat.
optionRationale.3: Dhaka hosted the founding summit but not the secretariat.

questions.stem: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 inserted Part IX into the Constitution and gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to urban local bodies. This amendment came into effect in 1993.

optionRationale.2: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 is known for the Preamble changes.
optionRationale.3: The 44th Amendment of 1978 removed the right to property from Part III.
optionRationale.4: The 74th Amendment deals with municipalities.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922.
Reason (R): The violence at Chauri Chaura in which policemen were killed went against the principle of non-violence.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and R is the reason. After a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922, Gandhi felt the country was not ready for non-violent mass action and withdrew the movement.

optionRationale.2: R is the actual reason for the withdrawal, so option 2 is too weak.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.stem: The Rajatarangini, a chronicle of the kings of a region, was written by Kalhana. It deals with the history of
questions.explanation: Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini in the twelfth century as a verse chronicle of the kings of Kashmir. It is considered one of the earliest Indian works that comes close to history writing.

optionRationale.1: It is not about Gujarat.
optionRationale.2: It is not about Bengal.
optionRationale.4: Vijayanagara is the subject of other sources.

questions.stem: The Cabinet Mission, which proposed a plan for the transfer of power, came to India in
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission of three British ministers arrived in March 1946 to discuss the transfer of power and proposed a three-tier federal structure. It was followed by the Constituent Assembly elections.

optionRationale.1: 1942 was the year of the Cripps Mission and Quit India.
optionRationale.3: 1944 is the year of the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.
optionRationale.4: 1947 is the year of the Mountbatten Plan and independence.

questions.stem: Which one of the following rivers originates in Tibet before entering India?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra rises near the Mansarovar region in Tibet, where it is called the Tsangpo, and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh. The Ganga rises in Uttarakhand, and the Godavari and Narmada rise within peninsular India.

optionRationale.1: The Ganga starts at Gangotri in Uttarakhand.
optionRationale.2: The Godavari starts near Nashik in Maharashtra.
optionRationale.3: The Narmada starts at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.
